hook.situation: Asking natural follow-up questions in Korean: what, where, when, why, how, who, how many, what kind, and which one.
objectives: Choose the question word that matches the missing information.
Keep the question word in the position where the answer would normally appear.
Use particles with question words: 어디에, 어디에서, 누구를, 누구랑, 몇 시에.
hook.whyItMatters: Good follow-up questions make conversation continue. If learners only memorize isolated words like 뭐 or 어디, they often ask unclear questions. This chapter connects each question word to the sentence role it actually fills.

grammarNotes.title: Question words (누구, 뭐, 어디, 언제, 왜, 어떻게, 몇, 얼마)
grammarNotes.func: Question words ask for one missing piece of info — who, what, where, when, why, how, how many, how much. The big thing: in Korean the question word sits in the exact spot the answer would go. It does not jump to the front like English 'where' or 'what' does.

formTable.add: 누구 + 가 → 누가 (subject); 누구 + 를 (object); 누구 + 예요
formTable.ex: 누가 와요? / 누구를 만나요? / 이 사람 누구예요?

formTable.add: 뭐 + 예요; 뭐 + 를 → 뭘 (object). 무엇 is the written form, rare in speech
formTable.ex: 이거 뭐예요? / 뭘 먹어요? / 뭐 해요?

formTable.add: 어디 + 예요; 어디 + 에 (where you go / where something is); 어디 + 에서 (where you do something)
formTable.ex: 집이 어디예요? / 어디에 가요? / 어디에서 일해요?

formTable.when: when / why / how — 언제, 왜, 어떻게
formTable.add: no particle — they work like adverbs on their own
formTable.ex: 언제 와요? / 왜 안 와요? / 어떻게 가요?

formTable.when: how many / how much — 몇 + counter, 얼마
formTable.ex: 몇 개예요? / 몇 시예요? / 이거 얼마예요?

examples.note: 누구 sits right where the answer goes: 제 친구예요 (It's my friend). Same slot, just swap the word.

examples.en: What do you eat for lunch?
examples.note: 뭘 (뭐+를) stays in the object slot before the verb. Answer 밥을 먹어요 fills the very same slot.
어디 takes 에서 because work happens there (an action). Answer 회사에서 일해요 keeps the same 에서.
얼마 is the normal word for asking a price. Answer 만 원이에요 drops right into the 얼마 spot.

keyPoint.label: The question word stays where the answer goes
keyPoint.body: English moves the question word up front: 'WHAT do you eat?' Korean leaves it in place, right before the verb: 뭐 먹어요? → 밥 먹어요. Look at the slot: 밥 먹어요 / 뭐 먹어요 — same spot, you just swap 밥 for 뭐. So think of the answer first, then drop the question word into its slot. (어디 still needs 에 or 에서 — that comes next.)

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 누구 + 가 squeezes down to 누가 (the 구 disappears, it doesn't just link). 뭐 + 를 squeezes to 뭘. 무엇을 links over the patchim and sounds like [무어슬].

drill.instruction: Turn each statement into a question. Swap the underlined answer for the matching question word and leave it in the same slot (keep the particle).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: From English, people want to swing the question word to the very front of the sentence (Where do you go?). In Korean it does not move up front and it never goes after the verb — it stays in the answer's slot, right before the verb. So it's 어디 가요?, not 가요 어디? and not 어디 가요 fronted away from its slot.

exampleSentence.note: Use 뭐 for things, actions, food, plans, or objects.

exampleSentence.en: Where are you going on the weekend?
exampleSentence.note: Pair 어디 with 에 for destination/location and 에서 for action place.
언제 asks for time without needing a counter.
왜 expects a reason, not a place or time answer.

exampleSentence.en: How do you memorize Korean words?
exampleSentence.note: 어떻게 asks method. For opinion, use 어때요?
Attach the role: 누구가 becomes 누가, but 누구를 and 누구랑 stay visible.

extendedVocabulary.english: how much; how long; to what degree

exampleSentence.en: How long does it take to get to work?
exampleSentence.note: 얼마나 asks about degree, distance, time length, or frequency.

exampleSentence.en: How many people are coming to the study group?
exampleSentence.note: 몇 needs a number word or counter such as 시, 명, 개, 번.

exampleSentence.en: What kind of music do you like?
exampleSentence.note: Use 무슨 before a noun when asking the kind, name, or category.

exampleSentence.en: Which cafe shall we meet at?
exampleSentence.note: Use 어느 when choosing among options the listener can imagine.

exampleSentence.en: If you have a question, please ask now.
exampleSentence.note: 질문 pairs naturally with 하다, 있다, and 물어보다.
대답 is a spoken or written reply to a question.
이유 helps expand 왜 questions into clearer follow-ups.
방법 helps turn 어떻게 into a fuller question about method.

extendedDialogue.setting: A learner asks follow-up questions after hearing that someone studies Korean online.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.grammarNote: 어디에서 asks for the action place.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: I learn at home through an online class.
lines.grammarNote: 집에서 marks where the learning happens; 온라인 수업으로 marks the means.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.grammarNote: The answer fills the time slot.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 한국 친구들과 더 편하게 이야기하고 싶어서요.
lines.romanization: hanguk chingudeulgwa deo pyeonhage iyagihago sipeoseoyo.
lines.en: Because I want to talk more comfortably with Korean friends.
lines.grammarNote: -고 싶어서요 gives the reason in a natural short answer.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: I watch dramas and repeat the sentences.
lines.grammarNote: The answer gives a concrete study method.

lines.speaker: 민서

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: I practice with my study group friends.
lines.grammarNote: 친구들이랑 fills the same companion slot as 누구랑.

readingText.title: A study-plan chat
readingText.body: 민서는 새 스터디에 들어가기 전에 지훈에게 여러 가지를 물어봤어요. 먼저 어디에서 모이는지 물었고, 지훈은 학교 앞 카페에서 만난다고 대답했어요. 민서는 몇 시에 시작하는지도 물었어요. 지훈은 토요일 두 시에 시작한다고 했어요. 민서가 왜 그 스터디를 만들었냐고 묻자, 지훈은 혼자 공부하면 자꾸 미뤄서 친구들과 같이 연습하고 싶었다고 했어요. 마지막으로 민서는 어떻게 준비하면 좋으냐고 물었고, 지훈은 짧은 자기소개와 질문 세 개를 준비하면 된다고 말했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Before joining a new study group, Minseo asked Jihoon several questions. She asked where they meet, what time they start, why he made the group, and how she should prepare. Jihoon answered each question with the missing place, time, reason, and method.

culturalNote.title: Follow-up questions should feel connected
culturalNote.body: In Korean conversation, a follow-up question often reuses the other person's topic instead of starting from zero. If someone says 한국어를 배워요, natural follow-ups are 어디에서요?, 언제부터요?, 왜요?, 어떻게 연습해요?, and 누구랑요?
culturalNote.tip: Short follow-ups with 요 can sound natural after the topic is already clear: 어디에서요? 왜요? 누구랑요?

inlineExercises.prompt: You want to ask where someone studies. Which form fits the action place?
inlineExercises.explanation: 공부하다 is an action, so the place of the action takes -에서.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which answer naturally responds to 왜 한국어를 공부해요?
options: 한국어를 공부한 지 두 달 됐어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 왜 expects a reason, often answered with -아서/어서요 or -고 싶어서요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Ask 'Who are you meeting today?' in Korean.
inlineExercises.explanation: The person you meet is the object, so 누구를 is the full form.

inlineExercises.prompt: Ask 'What time does class start?' using 몇.
inlineExercises.explanation: 몇 combines with 시 to ask for clock time.
Use 어땠어요 for 'How was it?' 어떻게 asks method, as in 어떻게 갔어요?
일하다 is an action, so the place where it happens takes 에서. 에 would fit a destination or static location, not work happening there.
얼마 asks about price. 이거 sets “this thing” as what you are asking about.
언제 asks for time and sits before the verb. Korean keeps the question word in the answer slot rather than moving it far away.
누구 + 가 always contracts to 누가 — 누구가 is not used in standard Korean. The correct subject question is 누가 와요?

inlineExercises.prompt: Which question asks about method or way?
inlineExercises.explanation: 어떻게 asks “how” or by what method. 언제 asks time, and 왜 asks reason.

bullets: Question words match the missing information: 뭐, 어디, 언제, 왜, 어떻게, 누구.
Particles still matter: 어디에, 어디에서, 누구를, 누구랑, 몇 시에.
몇, 무슨, and 어느 attach before nouns: 몇 명, 무슨 뜻, 어느 카페.
Best check: answer the question and see whether the answer fits the same slot.

writingTask.prompt: You just met someone new — write 3 short questions to keep the conversation going: ask where they live, what they do on weekends, and when they're free.
writingTask.hint: Put the question word in the answer's slot, with no inversion (어디 살아요? / 주말에 뭐 해요? / 언제 시간이 있어요?).
writingTask.model: 어디에 살아요? 주말에 보통 뭐 해요? 언제 시간이 있어요?
writingTask.modelEn: Where do you live? What do you usually do on weekends? When are you free?

canDo: Ask who, what, where with question words in the answer's slot (누구 · 뭐 · 어디)
Ask when and why without changing word order (언제 · 왜)
Ask how, how many, and how much (어떻게 · 몇 · 얼마나)
Ask follow-up questions that keep a conversation moving (질문 · 대답)
